title: The Ravel Nexus
notes: The Ravel faction: what every Ravel Commander builds on, and what the campaigns' raids are drawn from. The engine's bench Ravel roster is named by id (runners that burst, raiders, slingers, the Den and the Ravel Nexus); the Stash and the Chop Shop are defined here. Its buildings mirror the Citizens' at Ravel prices: the Den sends runners as the Barracks sends troopers, the Sling Pit slingers, the Stash is the Supply Depot, and the Chop Shop is the second tier, raiders as the Garrison's pikemen. A Citizen Commander who takes a card from the Ravel Nexus (Averno) requires it to see what that card brings. First guesses, no balance claim.

card.title: Stash
card.subtitle: Room for 8 more units
card.description: Scrap and fuel, piled where the crews can reach it. Lets your side field more units at once. It bursts when it falls.

content.notes: The Ravel Supply Depot: eight more units the side may field at once. Like everything Ravel, it bursts when it falls.

card.title: Sling Pit
card.subtitle: Sends slingers
card.description: A pit of loose scrap and the crews who throw it. Sends a wave of slingers each Battle Round.

content.notes: A second tier-1 producer, so a Ravel side chooses between quick melee and thrown range: slingers stay behind the runners and hit buildings over them.

card.title: Chop Shop
card.subtitle: Builds raiders
card.description: Where wrecks become raiders. Sends a wave of the heavy brawlers each Battle Round, once a Den stands.

content.notes: The Ravel second tier, the Garrison's mirror: it needs a Den standing as the Build Phase opens.

card.title: Fuse Shed
card.subtitle: Sends bombers
card.description: Where the crews pack scrap round a fuse. Sends two bombers each Battle Round, once a Den stands.

content.notes: The bomber's building, of the second tier after the Den as the Chop Shop is. A shed packed with charges bursts harder than a Den when it falls, as the Chop Shop does.

card.title: Bomber
card.subtitle: From your Fuse Shed
card.description: Runs at the thickest knot of enemy troops it can reach and bursts there, hurting everything round it, yours too. Never goes for a building.

content.notes: The owner's yes, 2026-10-21: it runs at the thickest knot of enemies and bursts there. As fast as a runner and as frail (20 health, a runner's speed and initiative), with no weapon: touching its target, it bursts (a contact detonation, triggerRange 1), and it bursts the same way if it is killed first. Radius 4 reaches 4 columns across and 2 rows up and down. 36 damage, where the proposal said about 30: a trooper (40) survives one burst and a runner (16) or a slinger (18) does not, so a block of troopers is hurt all over and a second bomber finishes it, and a loose line loses one or two. It aims at the enemy with the most of its side round it, not the nearest (aim: crowd), and hunts units and workers, never a building. First numbers, to be measured.

buildings.notes: The Ravel Barracks: five runners a wave for a little less than a Barracks's four troopers. A runner is two fifths of a trooper in health and bursts when it falls, so a Den's wave is cheaper and more fragile, and hurts what it dies against.
Three slingers a wave: thrown range, at the price of a Barracks and a bit.
The Supply Depot's mirror, at its price.
Three raiders a wave once a Den stands: the Garrison's mirror, a little cheaper and a little fewer.

Two bombers a wave once a Den stands, for a little more than a Den. A bomber has no weapon, so the duel's measure of strength (health times damage a second) counts it as none and no scripted player picks it yet: a player chooses it against a tight army. First numbers, to be measured.

powers.name: Scrap Rush
powers.description: Three runners join at your Nexus.
powers.notes: Reserve Callup's mirror: more bodies, each one less, and every one bursts.

powers.name: Hot Shift
powers.notes: Drill Schedule's mirror, on the Den.

powers.name: Short Fuses
powers.notes: The cascade, wider: a raider's blast reaches two tiles and hits harder.
